name: dsh-decompile
description: Reverse-engineering MCP for DeepSeek (DSH). 230+ native tools (PE / ELF / Mach-O / DEX / WASM / .NET / ASAR / GGUF / BEAM / Go), 60+ decompiler and debugger backend bridges, 6,000+ skills catalog. Returns structured findings with evidence and unknowns.
author: decompile maintainers

notes: DeepSeek does not yet have a standardized MCP config path. Point your DeepSeek client (API wrapper, CLI, or IDE extension) at the `mcpServers.decompile` block above.
If you use a DeepSeek-compatible OpenAI-style proxy, call `decompile serve` via stdio and bridge tool calls through the proxy's function-calling interface.
For direct DeepSeek API usage without an MCP client, run `decompile analyze <path>` and feed the JSON findings into your prompt as evidence.

categories: Dynamic instrumentation (Frida, Cheat Engine, Unicorn emulators)
Skill / agent / plugin / prompt catalog (FTS5 search)

promptingGuide.systemPrompt: You are a reverse-engineering agent that operates through the decompile MCP server. For every target: (1) identify format with file_identify / file_summary, (2) pick the right native parser + optional decompiler backend, (3) collect evidence with concrete tool calls before stating conclusions, (4) report findings in the shape {claim, evidence[{tool,ref,data}], confidence} with unknowns and limitations called out explicitly.

fewShotExamples.assistant: Running file_identify + pe_parse + pe_imports_json on /tmp/malware.bin, then smart_decompile on the entrypoint. Returning findings with address references and import list; any unknown behavior will be listed as 'unknowns' for the next probe.

fewShotExamples.user: What anti-debug does this driver use?
fewShotExamples.assistant: Searching the skills catalog with db_search 'anti-debug driver' first, then checking for known IOCTL patterns via pe_imports_json and string scan. Will cite each match with the tool and the line / RVA / signature that produced it.
